title: Bidirectional Dijkstra: Seattle in Half the Time
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra visualize two simultaneous shortest-path searches—one expanding from the start and one from the goal. On real street-map style graphs, the frontiers meet in the middle to reduce work while still guaranteeing optimal routes.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ Bidirectional Dijkstra in action—Seattle (South Lake Union) edition! 🌉

Instead of running a single-source Dijkstra that expands outward until it reaches the destination, Bidirectional Dijkstra runs **two Dijkstra searches at the same time**: 
➡️ one forward from the start node and 
⬅️ one backward from the goal node.

🧠 Graph-theory view: your street map becomes a **weighted graph** (intersections = nodes, roads = edges with travel costs like distance/time). Both searches use a **priority queue (min-heap)** to always expand the currently cheapest frontier, and they **terminate when the combined best-known path is no worse than any potential connection**—when the two wavefronts meet. ✅

📍Why it’s powerful on real maps: by narrowing the search region in large graphs, you often explore far fewer nodes than classic Dijkstra—while still preserving the **shortest-path optimality guarantee**.

fb_caption:
Seattle street maps become a weighted graph 🌐 and Bidirectional Dijkstra finds the shortest route by searching from both start and goal simultaneously. This reduces the explored area (often dramatically) by letting the two priority-queue frontiers meet, while still guaranteeing the optimal path.
